stemMd: What is the function of the third paragraph in the structure of the passage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It criticises the questionnaire results described in the first paragraph.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It qualifies the case for diaries by setting out their limits and a trade-off facing survey offices.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It supplies evidence that the working week is getting longer.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It repeats the second paragraph's description of diaries in plainer language.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It introduces a new method of collecting data that replaces the diary.

explanationMd:
Ask what the paragraph does relative to its neighbours. The second paragraph makes a positive case for diaries: they measure rather than summarise, and they capture simultaneous activities. The third opens with "None of this makes diaries the last word", a signal that the author is about to qualify what has just been said. It then gives limits (diaries are burdensome, volunteers tend to have spare time, one day is a poor guide to a varying schedule) and generalises to a trade-off between depth and coverage, noting that public debate has ignored it.

The fourth paragraph then draws the modest lesson. So the third paragraph is the counterweight in the middle: it keeps the case for diaries from being read as a verdict that diaries are simply better.

distractorRationale.e: No new method is introduced. The paragraph discusses limits of the diary and the choice between depth and coverage.
distractorRationale.a: The first paragraph's questionnaire findings are not criticised again here. The paragraph turns to the limits of diaries.
distractorRationale.c: The paragraph mentions the debate about the length of the working week only to show that it mixes different instruments. It offers no evidence either way.
distractorRationale.d: It adds new material (burden, volunteers, single days, the depth-coverage trade-off) instead of restating the description.

accessibilityText: A structure question about the time diaries passage. It asks for the function of the third paragraph. The five choices: it criticises the questionnaire results described in the first paragraph; it qualifies the case for diaries by setting out their limits and a trade-off facing survey offices; it supplies evidence that the working week is getting longer; it repeats the second paragraph's description of diaries in plainer language; it introduces a new data-collection method that replaces the diary.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Paragraph 3 turns from praise of diaries to their limits and the depth-versus-coverage trade-off, which qualifies the case for diaries. A misplaces the target, because the paragraph criticises diaries and public debate, not the questionnaire results. C is wrong because it criticises that debate. D is wrong because the content is new. E is wrong because no new method is introduced. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: Paragraph 3 limits the case for diaries: they are burdensome, their volunteers are self-selected, and a single day is a thin sample. It then sets out the depth-versus-coverage trade-off facing survey offices. A is wrong because the paragraph is about diaries' limits, not about questionnaires. C is wrong because the paragraph says the working-week debate ignores method, not that the week is getting longer. D is wrong because the paragraph adds new points rather than restating, and E is wrong because no new method is introduced.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the opening words "None of this" and the list of limits identify the paragraph as a qualification; the other choices misdescribe its content. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
